measurement.title: How Loud Is an Involving Hi-Fi Listening Session?

notes:
A high-quality Hi-Fi system can make music feel remarkably present — but how loud are we actually listening when we turn the volume up for a truly involving experience?
This measurement was taken during a listening session of Charlie Haden’s The Montreal Tapes: with Paul Bley and Paul Motian at a deliberately high playback level. The result was powerful and engaging, although still below the level I would consider realistic for recreating the scale and dynamics of a live performance.
Beyond evaluating the system, this measurement asks a different question: what level of sound exposure are we accumulating during serious music listening? SPL, listening duration and musical dynamics all matter when considering exposure; a short peak and an hour spent listening at an elevated average level are very different things.
For DSR, this is where Hi-Fi and measurement meet: not simply asking whether a system sounds good, but measuring the conditions under which we experience it. The same approach extends across playback setup, resonance, speed, vibration, room behaviour and acoustic level — turning subjective listening observations into something that can also be documented and compared.
Source: Eversolo A6 - HiRes 192KHz
Preamplifier: Audio Research SP20
Power Amplifiers: Manley Snapper
Speakers: Proac D28
